Michael Porter, a 42-year-old individual recently released from Manning Correctional Institution (June 1, 2026), completed his initial re-entry intake assessment. The session focused on identifying Michael's immediate structural barriers—including housing, transportation, and extensive legal/financial holds—and selecting an optimal program track to support his long-term recovery, mental health, and career placement goals.
## Participant Profile & Background
Housing Stability: Currently residing in an Oxford House (sober living environment) located on Dorchester Road.
Recovery Status: Maintaining continuous sobriety for approximately 4–5 years (initiated during his incarceration period); actively participating in AA/NA support groups.
Education & Vocational Credentials:
Does not currently hold a GED due to early-life learning disabilities and foster care disruptions.
Successfully earned Work Keys and WIN Certificates through vocational programming at Kershaw Correctional Institution.
Incarcerated Work History: Experienced in dairy farming (milking/production), industrial laundry operations, and institutional food service (Clarendon County).
Has workers comp issue from prison accident. 
Driver's License-Currently suspended with $1,000 in reinstatement fees due to outstanding state holds.
Child Support-Active hold and arrears case for his 11-year-old son; case was frozen during a past period of disability. A formal child support clearance is required to reinstate his driver's license.
Vocational Rehabilitation appointment scheduled for June 24 at 11:15 AM on Dorchester Road.
Relies entirely on public transit; requires immediate bus pass assistance to maintain program compliance.
Enrolled in WellVista for mental health medications (currently prescribed Zoloft and Remeron for severe anxiety, depression, and PTSD).
